To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the oxidised state of Yersinia pseudutuberculosis Tpx (ypTpx), in complex with the salicylidenediethylhydrazine inhibitor, reveals the binding mode of the inhibitor to the active site of ypTpx, and that the structural data were used for modelling the binding of the inhibitor to Tpx from Y.pseudotuberculosis.

(i) the structure of the oxidized form of ypTpx reveals a dimer interface that is similar to other atypical 2 Cys thiol peroxidas, and (ii) the structure of reduced ypTpx reveals that the active site of the protein is more open, and that the dimer interface is more flexible, compared with the oxidized form.
the structures of ypTpx in the oxidised, reduced and C61S mutant states are consistent with previously determined atypical 2 Cys peroxidases.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structures of ypTpx presented in this paper provide insights into the binding and mechanism of action of salicylidene compounds.
the structures of ypTpx in the oxidised, reduced and reduced mutant states provide insights into the binding modes of salicylidene-acylhydrazide antivirulence agents.

the salicylidenediacetamides bind to the oxidised state of ypTpx and the binding mode is consistent with the binding of salicylidene acetohydrazides to the reduced form of ypTpx, as previously proposed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structures of the oxidised and the reduced states of ypTpx are consistent with previously determined structures for atypical 2 Cys Tpxs.
the structural data obtained in this study provide a platform for the design of new salicylidene compounds with improved activity and selectivity for ypTpx.

the salicylidenediacetylhydrazide (SDH) compounds bind at the catalytic site of ypTpx in an extended conformation, with the hydrazide moiety binding to the catalytic site and the salicylidine moiety binding to a hydrophobic patch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of salicylidene compounds to ypTpx is likely to involve a combination of hydrophobic and hydrogen bonding interactions.

the structural data obtained on ypTpx, together with the solution structure data, provide insights into the binding modes of the compounds and the structural consequences of the compounds on the protein.
the binding of salicylidene compounds to ypTpx is not dependent upon the redox state.
